title: Exhortation to Moral Renewal
english: The Babylon captivity had taken hold, and through the passage of time, the incomplete and without confidence appeared in dishonor because of being seized by so many evils. But from the bringing forth of virtue and being instructed in philosophy, the first growth and being steadfast and deep in mind, in that very flower of the age, the control and judge of those elders was being shown. But let us see, if it seems to you, by bringing the word back to the beginning, how to be a friend to God is lofty and blessed.

When the city of Jerusalem was taken by war from the Assyrians, the peoples of the Hebrews then were dispersed to Babylon. And there was also the blessed Daniel, a multitude of spear-wielding youths, and a cheerful boy was recounting the war, a small and much-suffering people, having neither an occasion from his kinsmen to appear, nor being considered a worthy gain of war by the enemies; invisible, without glory because of age and because of misfortune; seen only by the one looking well.

For God alone saw the pure soul of the youth, just as a pearl enveloped in shell-like oysters or gold lying in the hollows of the earth; as a bride properly covered with the veils of the dais. And when the appointed time came and it was necessary for the hidden to be revealed, for the invisible to become known, for the despised to be looked upon, for the one hidden by the darkness of misfortune to shine, a little effusion of the Spirit, and the humble of all to be higher; wise he who does not divide the mouth; a judge of hidden things; a critic of judges; sitting on a high throne, having not yet become a servant of courts; the young man avenging temperance being slandered, turning back a wandering people, calling back the vote of the whole city having been wrongly cast.
Listen...

Therefore, hold fast your soul to the reading and to the wonder in every way. And I, having left aside the matters of other books, which the psalms have profitably sung to us with pleasure, which the apostle advised, and which the Lord has masterfully legislated in the gospels, have been drawn to this history.
For I see two youths of excellence: one in the act of judging, and the other in the act of being judged; and Daniel being struck with votes, and Susanna being crowned with the victory of temperance.

Come then, if it seems good, you lovers of beautiful things and of virtue, let us renew the ancient judgment by memory; let us cut away the present lawlessness with ancient temperance, having stepped in as elders, admiring a maidenhood that has become old and a youth that has become urbanized. O defiled elders and leaders of the people, who desire to join those joined by the law of marriage, needing ten thousand teachers for restoration, lurking in temperance, schemers of deceits, quick finders of slander!

You were the ones judging fornication with your lips and condemning adultery; being doctors of others and becoming the disease themselves; being tombs struck full within of uncleanness and beautifying the outward appearance. The high ones, sitting upon the thrones of judges, when you invited lawlessness by creeping into the thickets of plants and shrubs.

Then the accuser of transgressions and the counselor of evils laughed seeing you, how those at the top of the people, the eloquent and the chosen, have drawn near to the land like certain wall-burrowers or robbers, in order to behold an uncontrolled spectacle; and you hid yourselves in the shrubs according to the thickets, which from the tangled and shady places house the birds and unexpectedly leap upon the dwellers.
O, what a similar evil, which the destroyer of human souls from the beginning unto...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Corruption of the Court and the Appeal to God
english: The end is fitting! In Paradise, the first fall of the exalted man occurred; in Paradise also now the elders, being worked by the serpent, fall away from the original glory, becoming condemned instead of judges, workers not of life but of sin.

But there, the man prevailed, while the woman was defeated, and the emptiness of the first woman found no maiden upon the Babylonian. And one could rightly say that Babylon is not a confusion because of Susanna, but a keeping of God's commandments, a guard of temperance, a city of a manly woman, a place of a triumphal feast.

This I, having ascended through the middle times, lead to Joseph by the likeness of virtue toward the world; but I set the honorable woman beside the temperate one who is a friend of God, beside the child of Israel. I place one and the same crown upon both, the one for temperance; and I cast down the defeated ones beneath the feet of the victors: to Joseph, the unrestrained Egypt, the mistress of the free slave; but to Susanna, the dishonorable elders.

I set these as teachers of temperance: the one of womanhood, the other of the youth of men; lamps of the inhabited world, flowers of the resurrection, judges of adultery, guardians of lawful marriages. Finally, let us occupy ourselves only with the sacred woman's account; for now Joseph is an episode and the temperate one is a parenthesis of temperance.

Because the elders, as they thought, had the hunt within nets, and stepped out from the thicket to take prey immediately, they did not find the most cowardly deer, but one standing against them both and against the dragon who is the cause of these things, but a deer-slayer animal; and the account rightly found the image of the animal: they enticed, but were not heard; they threatened, but did not strike terror.
Therefore the wicked are helpless and are held by two great things...

By chance of desire and fear of rebuke. But filthy sums of money seize slander, and for a solution to evil they find another evil, and they prepare a cover for adultery through murder. For a sinner, when he falls into the beginnings of transgressions, like a splinter at the start, he drags along the following lawlessness. And he happens to beget of the good things the good, and of the bad things the similar.

Therefore also now murder is the fruit of adultery, and a council sits in haste as if upon a great injustice against the woman, and a crowd is led away having the one being judged as a spectacle. And the accusers and the judges are the same; and many a slandering person was deemed trustworthy, and a youth being slandered was condemned from the prevailing suspicion.

And a people, being tossed about and suffering—for a people is accustomed to be struck by impulse—was driven astray in indignation and was carried along by the impulse of the elders; the parents of the one being judged wailed, the husband suffered the calamity, the children wailed from here and there, being distraught because of the mother's danger, and the race was covered by shame.

But the good judges, the fellow-combatants of temperance, commanded her, having her dignity solemnly covered by a garment—for she, possessing decorum, had rushed to be naked—not even regarding the confusion of evils, so that in the court of adultery, they might perform adultery against the adultery, giving rest to the shameful desire by the sight of the one being judged. And they placed hands upon the head, which was a symbol of condemnation, using a clean body; the unrestrained ones, through touch and through it, were proselytizing the lie, while the good ones are defenders of the truth.

And as the people were subdued and the vote was cast and the punishment was near, the one being slandered then looked up to the judge of judges; she brought the legal case from men to God, making an appeal to the Unaccountable.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Judgment and the Pattern of Holiness
english: A courtroom, and the truth was not delayed.

Therefore, arise to me, O blessed Daniel, and now by the word as you were awakened, and then by the Spirit; say also that you are innocent of this blood, just as Pilate later [did] against the raving Hebrews. Analyze the people upon the criterion; give a beginning to the justice that has been badly completed; set the false judges to be judged; let the order of the protectors be changed, and let the woman observe the elders, just as she herself a little while ago was a spectacle of the city.

Let the captive judge the citizens; the stranger the locals; the youth the old. Use a holy mouth for the Spirit; for you do not have unclean lips, as Isaiah says of himself reviling himself; nor do you need one of the Seraphim or the cleansing coal. Depart wisely from the false judges, so that they may not also leap upon your own questions as a woman [leaps] in paradise.

For how we may clearly learn the beginning of the words of the thrice-blessed child: Having grown old through days of evil, now your sins, which you did formerly, have come to you, condemning the innocent and releasing the guilty. O the wonder and the great liberty of the Spirit! For where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

See, for it does not even hold back in the preambles; but, piercing into the depth of the conscience and seeing the souls of the elders as storehouses of sins, it seeks neither witness nor proofs; but is insulted and reviled with insolence, because the prophet has the decision written upon his chest.

And as far as it reached him, he would not even have said anything, but he sent them away unreservedly to the punishment; so that he might convince a foolish people and empty judges of the city, who accuse but do not judge according to the truth, and he brings to them the experience of questioning, separated from the truth and the falsehood of the [discourse]...

Mindful of the response, he exposes; and having brought forth the judgment, he does not give accountability to humans, but calls angels to be tormentors against them. For the dignity of the saints has grown to such an extent that they have invisible powers serving them.

What then happens to the defiled? Judgment was prepared; and they went away, giving the penalty through death for the old lawlessness and the new sin; and all Babylon had the paradox of what was happening through the mouth, and they blasphemed God with hymns, having made public the knowledge of the hidden deeds. And Hezekiah was refreshed rejoicing over the daughter; Joachim made a triumph for the feast of the wife; and twenty-nine children, legitimate and of temperate offspring, smile with faces surrounding the mother, and the much-teared grief was transformed into joy.

You, however, the people of Christ, most pious and soul-benefiting, having heard these histories, do not let the hearing pass by indifferently, but make the word a training and discipline for your own life. Women, emulate Susanna; thus guard toward men the temperance as she did toward herself; she accepted to suffer and to be in danger rather than to defile her life with adultery. Adultery provokes God, shames a man, destroys house and hearth, and works uncertain children. You elders, hate such old men; you rulers, fear the end of the lawless judges.

You young people, imitate the young man, so that in this way every age may be formed into the pattern of beautiful character, so that the whole fullness of the church may become holy and well-pleasing in Christ Jesus our Savior, to whom belong glory, might, and honor, with the co-ruling Father and with His all-holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always and unto the ages of ages. Amen.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
